goldens.comment: In .topic-meta-data h5 a, the original code had color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) but was changed to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). The lightness for the light theme changed from 30% to 70%, which is a dramatic inversion

This change for desktop/user.css changes $primary from 30% to 50% for the light theme; most other changes preserve the original $primary value and move the complement to $secondary for dark. Consider reviewing this (also applies to a similar .name change in the mobile variant).
In topic-post.css the original code used $lightness: 70% but the replacement uses $lightness: 30% for the light theme. This makes the text significantly darker than intended.

The light theme color for `.topic-meta-data h5 a` was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, which may unintentionally reduce contrast and affect readability. This change should be reviewed to ensure it aligns with design intentions.
In mobile/user.scss line 497, the lightness value for dark themes should be inverted to 70% instead of being changed to 50%. This change may lead to unintended visual regressions in light themes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss:102 — Light-theme styling changed from `70%` lightness to `30%`; it should retain `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the change at line 102 in mobile/modal.scss: from `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%);` to `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%));`. The finding correctly identifies that the light-theme value changed from 70% to 30% lightness. Looking at other similar changes in the diff, the pattern is typically to keep the same lightness value for the light theme (first argument) and use a complementary value for dark theme. For example, in other files we see patterns like `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. This change appears to have swapped the values incorrectly - the light theme should retain 70% lightness on $primary, not 30%.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss:182 — The `h3` light-theme styling changed from `20%` lightness to `50%`, causing an unintended color regression.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in mobile/topic-post.scss line 182, the h3 color changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The finding correctly identifies that the light-theme value changed from 20% to 50% lightness, which is inconsistent with other similar changes in the codebase where the light-theme value typically remains the same. This appears to be an unintended regression where the lightness value was accidentally changed during the dark-light-choose conversion.
